members.name: Wenna Dunmore
members.detail: Big, fair, red-armed woman of the top farm in a brown wool dress; carried in on a sheep hurdle by Hew and another man, fighting and clawing at her collar, talking fast about the hens. Jaina's holding ward puts her to sleep (her chest rises, lines round her mouth let go). Buys store flour since the wet barley at harvest and eats 'the heel standing up'; early (a fist, gut only); by morning her forehead is 'only warm, a sleeper's warmth'.

members.name: Hew Dunmore
members.detail: Her husband, of the top farm (his barley had the wet in the ear 'black in the ear'); big and fair; sits on the floor holding her hand in both of his; wants to know if she is dead.

members.name: Col
members.detail: Smith's striker, lodging over the forge; the young man in his shirt and boots by the door; on the hill pasture all summer with his mother's oatmeal and oatcakes; two nights of bread and dripping since coming down; smallest knot of all ('no bigger than a walnut'); calls Tobin an old woman; at dawn on his feet, starving, going home.

members.name: The cooper's household
members.detail: Five in the house; two down so far (boy of ten, 'hot since yesterday', and his mother, hot since the day before; three more in the house and a bed kept for each); two loaves of Ellen's mam's bread a day plus bread with everything; a fist and more. The boy picks a scab on his knee to the blood; Jaina bandages it with her own knot ('Did you just *bite* my bandage?').

members.name: Mag and her mother (egg stall)
members.detail: Little girl five or six in a knitted cap pulled to her eyebrows, cheeks red as scrubbed brick, sagging on her mother's hip in a blue apron, coughing a small wet cough; 'Stand up, Mag, you're not a sack of turnips. Nearly done.' Not read by Jaina; likely early/unknown. Mother later puts her hand up flat at the departure.

members.name: Piers, the Aldon boys, the Hallams, the alehouse
members.detail: Piers: the militiaman with the pitchfork; sent house to house. Aldon boys: Brask's volunteers. The Hallams and the alehouse: received Joss's flour; Hallams' cart turned at the ford, alehouse had two sacks.

members.name: Unnamed
members.detail: Egg woman (calls her price, laughs); a woman haggling in a blue apron; a man selling salt herring from a barrel; two women at the pump; a man coughing in a doorway; someone coughing behind an upstairs shutter; a little girl in a man's coat down to her ankles who sits by the font holding a shawl over her mouth and takes it away when Wenna sleeps; Hew; the two men with the hurdle ('Hew' and one more).

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Recover; burn the bread; wake to oats.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Wary; the egg woman stops setting out her trestle; the blue-apron woman lifts her hand flat in what looks like thanks.

knowledge.detail: A fortnight/week/'however long it had been' ago this was Millhaven with smoke; the village is running a working market with a hammer, a bakehouse smoke haze, shutters up on three houses, a horseshoe points down over a lintel, a stool with a cup on a step left for someone who would not come out.

arc.currentPosition: Alive. Brask's village burned its bread.
